findings.statement: reader memory is independent of key count
a reader's index costs less than 32 bytes per key
findings.detail: 135 bytes per key resident, per reader process, shared with nobody

findings.statement: eight concurrent reader processes can hold a 10M-key store on this machine
findings.detail: at 135 B/key one reader fills 15.7GB of RAM at 124.6M keys; eight readers reach that at 15.6M keys each

notes: In RUM terms this is the memory spent to buy read performance. Spending it is a legitimate choice; the objection is that it is unmeasured, and that it is paid per process when the stated architecture is many reader processes sharing one mapping
